issues.issue: The duty is triggered by 'discovery' of a breach that 'materially and adversely affects the interests of the Certificateholders' and requires only 'prompt written notice', none of which is defined or given a time limit or consequence.

This notice paragraph sits inside Section 2.03, whose heading and subsection (b) address only the representations of the Master Servicer and Securities Administrator, yet it governs breaches of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements enforced under Section 2.02(d).

The closing sentence bars any substitution after the second anniversary of the Closing Date 'notwithstanding anything herein or in any other agreement to the contrary', while Section 2.05(a) postpones substitutions until a default occurs or an Opinion of Counsel is delivered, with no time limit.

The deposit date runs from the month 'during which the related Seller or the related Originator became obligated to repurchase or replace' the loan, without saying whether that obligation arises on breach, on discovery, or on demand.

The survival clause ties 'the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03' to 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', but Section 2.03's representations are corporate representations of Wells Fargo unconnected to loan delivery.
The sentence omits the connector before 'the Depositor had good title', so whether the Depositor warrants present title or merely recites a past state of affairs 'following the transfer' is unclear.

The trigger reads 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach', omitting the conjunction and leaving whose discovery starts the notice duty uncertain; the survival is also limited to 'the immediately preceding paragraph'.
The bar on repurchase applies to any loan 'that is not in default or as to which default is not reasonably foreseeable', a forward-looking standard with no benchmark or decision-maker identified.

The provision opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and can postpone a repurchase or substitution indefinitely, which cannot be squared with Section 2.03's absolute bar on substitutions after the second anniversary of the Closing Date.
The substitution option is conditioned on 'the conditions in Section 2.03 ... with respect to substitutions', but Section 2.03 states no substitution conditions other than the two-year cut-off.

The permitted purposes end with catch-alls — activities 'necessary, suitable or convenient' and 'such other activities as may be required' — and the closing sentence trails off with 'and this Section 2.07', leaving the limit on the Trust's powers uncertain.

The final sentence — no obligation on the Trustee to assume the duties of Wells Fargo or the Master Servicer 'unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer' — is a double negative that inverts the intended condition.
The bond and policy need only be 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees', a market standard with no stated amount or benchmark.
The paragraph provides for a 'request for release' but then imposes the return obligation by reference to 'Such trust receipt', a document that appears nowhere else in the sentence or the Agreement.

The access sentence is grammatically broken — 'to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — so who is entitled to access is not determinable from the text.

Deposits are made 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.04' and withdrawals 'pursuant to Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04', but Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex and governs neither deposits of insurance proceeds nor withdrawals.
The Master Servicer need only use 'its best reasonable efforts' to keep primary mortgage insurance in force, a hybrid standard that mixes two different efforts benchmarks.
Collections are directed 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05', but the Agreement contains no Section 5.05; Article V ends at Section 5.04.
Foreclosure is required only for loans 'as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection of delinquent payments', a standard with no measure and no decision-maker named.

This section gives the Master Servicer the Master Servicing Fee and, separately, 'all income and gain realized from any investment of funds in the Distribution Account ... during the Master Servicer Float Period', while the Master Servicing Fee definition already includes those float earnings.
